datasets_catalog.description: Source matrix for the Planetary Analog Explorer. A dataset is marked verified only when a validated manifest exists in this repository and its provenance fields were copied from that manifest or an official source. Planned and unverified sources carry no measurements and must not appear as observations.

status_legend.verified: Validated manifest exists; derived observations are committed.
status_legend.in_progress: Pipeline work exists but no validated manifest at this revision.
status_legend.not_verified: Source identified, access or validation not completed.
status_legend.planned: Interface-only; no pipeline, manifest, or measurement.

datasets.provider: European Space Agency (ESA) / Airbus Defence and Space; AWS Open Data mirror
datasets.title: Copernicus DEM GLO-90 Digital Surface Model (DSM), 3 arc-second COG
datasets.coverage: 113 observed 1.98 km windows in 12 sampling envelopes plus the original five; sparse indexed subset, not a global survey.
datasets.vertical_reference: EGM2008 heights in metres (manifest source notes)
datasets.temporal: 2021 product release; source WorldDEM-90 acquisitions 2010-2018 per the required attribution text.
datasets.license: Copernicus DEM GLO-90: free basis for the general public (AWS Open Data registry), under the Copernicus Contributing Mission Data Access Licence terms
datasets.attribution: Produced using Copernicus WorldDEM-90 © DLR e.V. 2010-2014 and © Airbus Defence and Space GmbH 2014-2018 provided under COPERNICUS by the European Union and ESA; all rights reserved.
datasets.access: Public, unsigned HTTPS Cloud Optimized GeoTIFFs mirrored at s3://copernicus-dem-90m (eu-central-1). The importer performs bounded GDAL range reads and does not download full tiles.
datasets.redistribution: Derived numeric values are committed with attribution and the verified licence link. Raw tiles and local crops are not committed.
datasets.limitations: Digital surface model: buildings, infrastructure, and vegetation are included. No nodata value is declared in source metadata. Each 2 km window is a local sample, not a characterization of the named region.

datasets.title: ESA WorldCover 10 m 2021 v200 land cover
datasets.coverage: 11 context-only class fractions for all 113 indexed Earth windows; static 2021 map, not a global survey.
datasets.temporal: Static annual 2021 epoch; annual composite without a confirmed per-pixel date.
datasets.attribution: Zanaga, D., Van De Kerchove, R., Daems, D., De Keersmaecker, W., Brockmann, C., Kirches, G., Wevers, J., Cartus, O., Santoro, M., Fritz, S., Lesiv, M., Herold, M., Tsendbazar, N.E., Xu, P., Ramoino, F., Arino, O., 2022. ESA WorldCover 10 m 2021 v200. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.7254221
datasets.access: Public, unsigned HTTPS range requests from the AWS Open Data bucket s3://esa-worldcover (eu-central-1), prefix v200/2021/map/, 3-degree tiles named ESA_WorldCover_10m_2021_v200_<N|S>dd<W|E>ddd_Map.tif.
datasets.redistribution: Derived class-fraction values are committed with CC BY 4.0 attribution. Raw WorldCover rasters are not committed.
datasets.limitations: Context only: not mineralogy, geology, a terrain measurement, or a similarity feature. The published independent validation reports 76.7% overall accuracy for 2021 v200. Helper classes group surfaces (for example bare/sparse vegetation). Small AOIs can be dominated by one class.

datasets.provider: NASA GSFC Planetary Geodesy Data Archive (PGDA) / LRO-LOLA
datasets.title: LRO-LOLA 5 m/pix surface-interpolated DEM, Shackleton rim (Site04)
datasets.coverage: 4 ROI-centred 1.98 km reference windows; windows may overlap.
datasets.source_crs: South polar stereographic in metres (full source WKT is stored in the manifest).
datasets.vertical_reference: Metres in the product's lunar reference frame (MOON_ME/DE421 per product documentation).
datasets.temporal: Product referenced by Barker et al. (2021); the raster acquisition epoch is not asserted in the manifest.
datasets.license: CC0-1.0 (NASA-led mission data per the NASA Science Data Portal; the PGDA page requests citation and carries no restrictive notice)
datasets.attribution: Barker, M.K., et al. (2021), Improved LOLA Elevation Maps for South Pole Landing Sites: Error Estimates and Their Impact on Illumination Conditions, Planetary & Space Science 203, 105119, doi:10.1016/j.pss.2020.105119.
datasets.access: Public HTTPS download from NASA PGDA; bounded HTTP range requests for the ROI. No credentials required.
datasets.redistribution: Derived numeric values are committed. The full 40,980,806-byte raster and local crops are not committed.
datasets.limitations: About 90% of 5 m pixels are interpolated from roughly 10% direct returns; median RMS Z error is about 0.30-0.50 m and median RMS slope error about 1.5-2.5 degrees. Do not treat 5 m texture as an independent measurement. The 90 m analysis window is a local reference sample.

datasets.provider: NASA PDS Geosciences Node / MGS MOLA
datasets.title: Mars Orbiter Laser Altimeter (MOLA) gridded topography (MEGDR)
datasets.coverage: Global median topography grids (16 ppd file; 128 ppd tiles). No bounded ROI was selected or processed.
datasets.source_crs: Equirectangular, planetocentric, positive east, sphere R = 3396000 m
datasets.vertical_reference: Planetary radius minus the GMM3 (mgm1025) areoid, metres
datasets.temporal: MOLA observations 1997-09-15 to 2001-06-30; static derived grid
datasets.access: Public PDS4 bundle. Metadata (33,177,600-byte MEG016 product; 129,761,280-byte MEG128 tile) was inspected, but no raster was downloaded or processed.
datasets.redistribution: not_verified; the PDS4 bundle label does not state a redistribution licence.
datasets.limitations: MEGDR native support is 3.704 km/pixel at 16 ppd and 0.463 km/pixel at 128 ppd, coarser than the 90 m terrain method, and no-observation bins are interpolated. No Mars MOLA reference value is claimed. Current Mars observations use the separately catalogued Jezero CTX DEM.

This importer read a bounded window via HTTP range requests and cached a small derived GeoTIFF; dataset checksum is the SHA-256 of that cached window, not of the full 40.98 MB (40,980,810 bytes) product. Citation: Barker, M.K., et al. (2021), Improved LOLA Elevation Maps for South Pole Landing Sites: Error Estimates and Their Impact on Illumination Conditions, Planetary & Space Science 203, 105119, doi:10.1016/j.pss.2020.105119. Batch checksum covers canonical reference records with window checksums. Published error statistics are site/ROI dependent; not per-window uncertainty estimates.

datasets.limitations: NASA PGDA LRO-LOLA product 'Site11_final_adj_5mpp_surf' (NASA GSFC Planetary Geodesy Data Archive (PGDA) / LRO-LOLA); 3200x3200 px, 5.0 m/pix, float32, nodata=NaN, striped 1x3200 blocks, uncompressed, overviews=none. Product documentation: MOON_ME reference frame of DE421, south polar stereographic X/Y in metres, pixel-registered GMT convention. The product page states that about 90% of the 5 m pixels are interpolated because LOLA cross-track/inter-spot spacing leaves only about 10% direct returns; median RMS Z error is about 0.30-0.50 m and median RMS slope error about 1.5-2.5 degrees. Track geolocation uncertainty is about 10-20 cm horizontally and 2-4 cm vertically. This importer read a bounded window via HTTP range requests and cached a small derived GeoTIFF; dataset checksum is the SHA-256 of that cached window, not of the full 40.98 MB (40,980,806 bytes) product. Citation: Barker, M.K., et al. (2021), Improved LOLA Elevation Maps for South Pole Landing Sites: Error Estimates and Their Impact on Illumination Conditions, Planetary & Space Science 203, 105119, doi:10.1016/j.pss.2020.105119. Batch checksum covers canonical reference records with window checksums. Published error statistics are site/ROI dependent; not per-window uncertainty estimates.

blockers: Moon PCP is a multi-year composite at one local-time bin, not a single acquisition or same-sol time series.

Mars THEMIS TI has no per-pixel uncertainty or QA layer; absolute accuracy is ~20%.
Mars THEMIS TI retrieval does not correct atmospheric clouds, surface slopes or subsurface ice/bedrock.
No cross-body D03 score; Earth NASA POWER context is unchanged.

limitations: Two neutron products and one radar mosaic only; this is not global or exhaustive Moon/Mars coverage.
Native source grids are preserved: 0.5 degree (Moon hydrogen), 236.9 m (Mini-RF), 4 degree (Mars neutron). Nothing is resampled to 90 m.
The Lunar Prospector product is a PDS special product that the PDS page describes as not a peer-reviewed archive; it is bounded to the 1998-1999 low-altitude mission phase.
The Mars HEND label has no start/stop dates; the 55-day mapping interval is documented in the product description, not the label.
Neutron-derived water-equivalent hydrogen and normalized epithermal flux are hydrogen evidence, not ice fraction, ice phase, or mineable ice.
Mini-RF CPR at or above unity is ice-consistent but not diagnostic; roughness and wavelength-scale rocks also raise CPR.
All 23 existing reference windows are coarser than the native source cells for the neutron products, so no AOI-scale ice detection is claimed.
No D04 similarity feature, D04 score, or cross-body water score is produced.
Raw products and window bytes remain in the gitignored var/cache/water-44 cache and are not committed.
non_claims: No ice fraction, ice volume, or mineable-ice estimate.
No water-equivalent hydrogen for Mars (the HEND map is a normalized flux, not WEH).
No detection claim at 1.98 km support from 0.5 or 4 degree neutron cells.
No hydrate or mineral abundance (D02 owns hydrated-mineral evidence).
No global coverage and no claim that an unmeasured area is ice-free.
notes: Counts are measured from the committed observations.jsonl, not estimated.
Every native read is recorded in plan.json and every window checksum in assets.json.
Source and candidate statuses are recorded in sources.json.

kernels.purpose: Leap-second kernel for UTC -> ephemeris time conversion.
Text planetary constants: body radii and IAU_MARS orientation.
JPL DE421 planetary ephemeris (1900-2050), Sun/Moon/Mars states.
Lunar frame definitions: MOON_ME / MOON_PA realized from DE421.

limitations: Model-derived geometry only: not observed irradiance, radiance, shadow fraction, or ionizing radiation.
Flat biaxial-ellipsoid tangent-plane normal; no DEM terrain horizon, horizon mask, observer height, or atmospheric/cloud model.
The site is placed on the reference biaxial ellipsoid; source DEM elevations and observer heights are not added.
Sun position is the light-time-corrected body-centre vector from SPICE; site parallax is applied by vector subtraction.
Point sites at existing reference coordinates; not a spatial average over the existing 1.98 km DEM windows.

Moon uses the MOON_ME body-fixed frame realized from DE421; Mars uses IAU_MARS from pck00011. Source projected-CRS coordinates are interpreted in those frames; prime-meridian/frame registration is a documented assumption, not an independent geodetic validation.
One documented instant only; no time series, eclipse/occultation, or local-solar-time series is produced.
DE421 covers approximately 1900-2050; kernel SHA-256 digests are pinned and any drift is rejected by the builder.
No cross-body D05 score; illumination and ionizing radiation remain separate subgroups. No Gy/Sv value is produced.
Kernels are cached under a gitignored var/cache directory and are not committed to Git.
non_claims: No observed solar irradiance or radiance.
No shadow fraction, shadow mask, or horizon visibility interval.
No ionizing radiation, absorbed dose (Gy), or equivalent dose (Sv).
No global or exhaustive Moon/Mars illumination coverage.
No cross-body or Earth/Moon/Mars D05 similarity score.
notes: Bounded pilot at existing Moon/Mars terrain reference coordinates only.
The values are a solar-geometry model, not a measurement of surface illumination.
Kernel URLs, SHA-256 digests, frame names, epoch, site coordinates, and limitations are preserved in this manifest.
Kernels are public NAIF products; redistribution of the kernel bytes is not re-asserted here.
